title: Blind corner at aisle end near yellow barriers
location: Center-left area where the main aisle meets the cross-aisle blocked by yellow barriers and orange water-filled barriers
observation: A blind corner exists where the main travel path intersects with a cross-aisle. The intersection is partially blocked by yellow expandable barriers and orange water-filled barriers (visible in E022, E023). Pedestrians are observed walking through this area (E002, E003, E004, E005, E006, E007, E008, E009, E010, E011). A wheeled vehicle entering from the blocked cross-aisle would be completely hidden from view by the barriers and the stacked pallets to the left. Conversely, pedestrians walking through the intersection would not see an approaching vehicle until it was very close.
risk_interpretation: A vehicle entering the main aisle from the blocked cross-aisle could collide with pedestrians who have no warning. This is a high-risk scenario as pedestrians are observed using this path.
recommended_actions: Install a convex mirror at the corner to provide visibility of the blocked cross-aisle; Mark a stop line before the intersection and require a horn signal before proceeding; Consider removing or repositioning the barriers to improve visibility; Implement a designated pedestrian crossing with clear markings
unknowns: Vehicle traffic frequency and speed in this area; Site rules regarding horn use at intersections

title: Pedestrian path blocked by stacked pallets and crates
location: Left side of the warehouse where stacked pallets and a large wooden crate narrow the pedestrian path
observation: A large stack of wooden pallets and a large wooden crate (visible in E014, E015, E028, E030) create a narrow passage for pedestrians. The yellow painted line on the floor indicates a designated path, but the physical obstructions force pedestrians to walk close to the edge of the marked area. If a wheeled vehicle were to operate in this area, pedestrians would have limited space to move out of the way and would be hidden from view by the stacked materials.
risk_interpretation: Pedestrians are at risk of being struck by vehicles due to the narrow passage and limited visibility. The stacked materials create a blind spot for both pedestrians and vehicle operators.
recommended_actions: Reposition the stacked pallets and crate to widen the pedestrian path; Install physical barriers to separate pedestrian and vehicle traffic; Mark the pedestrian path with additional signage; Implement a slow zone with a spotter if vehicles must operate in this area
unknowns: Vehicle traffic in this specific area; Whether the stacked materials are temporary or permanent

title: Blind spot at right-side aisle end near stacked boxes
location: Right side of the warehouse where stacked cardboard boxes and wooden crates create a blind corner
observation: A large stack of cardboard boxes and wooden crates (visible in E018, E019, E020, E021, E024, E025, E031) creates a blind corner on the right side of the warehouse. A pedestrian is seen walking behind these stacks in E019, disappearing from view. A wheeled vehicle entering from the right would not see the pedestrian until it was too late, and the pedestrian would not see the vehicle until it was very close.
risk_interpretation: A vehicle entering from the right could collide with a pedestrian who is hidden by the stacked materials. This is a medium-risk scenario as pedestrians are observed using this path.
recommended_actions: Install a convex mirror at the corner to provide visibility of the blind area; Mark a stop line before the corner and require a horn signal before proceeding; Reposition the stacked materials to improve visibility; Implement a designated pedestrian crossing with clear markings
unknowns: Vehicle traffic frequency and speed in this area; Site rules regarding horn use at intersections
